definition: Answering questions over a large personal or organizational archive of heterogeneous documents — the “memex” vision of an associative memory machine.
details: Answering questions over a large personal or organizational archive of heterogeneous documents — the “memex” vision of an associative memory machine. It anticipates modern retrieval-augmented QA.

explainer.lead: Answering questions over a large personal or organizational archive of heterogeneous documents, following the memex vision of an associative memory machine. It anticipates modern retrieval-augmented question answering.

tiers.eli5: Asking questions of your own giant pile of mixed documents, like a personal library that can answer you back.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build it by combining retrieval over heterogeneous archives with question answering, much as retrieval-augmented QA does today.
tiers.paperLevel: Answering questions over a large personal or organizational archive of heterogeneous documents — the memex vision of an associative memory machine; it anticipates modern retrieval-augmented QA.

explainer.example: A user asks a question and the system answers from an organization's mixed collection of documents.
